title: Bug Report: Unintended Vertical Snap on Single Click with Custom-Framed Apps and FancyZones Padding Thresholds
author: oldhandben

status.label: Needs maintainer reproduction with a custom-frame app
status.detail: The report already isolates low-padding and custom-window-frame conditions, but the current code and test coverage do not prove whether FancyZones placement or native Windows snap hit testing is the dominant cause.

next_action.label: Reproduce the border click on an ultrawide layout
next_action.reason: A local repro against the exact geometry is more valuable than another generic request for logs.

judgment.rationale: The issue provides concrete padding thresholds, a specific custom-framed app example (Opera), and a reliable symptom triggered by a single border click. That is enough for maintainer-side reproduction even though the fix boundary between FancyZones placement and native Windows snap remains uncertain.
evidence: At 1 px padding the reporter says all apps trigger a vertical maximize on a single bottom-border click; at 5 px, standard apps recover but custom-framed apps such as Opera still fail.
Disabling native Windows Snap eliminates the problem entirely, while FancyZones Override Windows Snap does not.
The report is on an ultrawide monitor and says the zone top edge is at the top of the screen.
Current FancyZones tests cover layout spacing and keyboard snap behavior, but no focused coverage exists for custom-framed bottom-border clicks after zone placement.
judgment.recommended_action: Run a focused local repro with an ultrawide-style layout and a custom-framed app before publishing a fix hypothesis.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys change may be needed, but the current public evidence does not yet isolate whether FancyZones should adjust geometry, snap override policy, or nothing at all.

issue_context.summary: FancyZones-placed windows can vertically maximize on a single bottom-border click when the zone is flush to the top of the monitor, especially for custom-framed applications. The report is detailed enough to reproduce, but not yet to select a code change.
known_information: The reporter is on PowerToys 0.100.2 with an ultrawide setup on Windows 11 25H2.
At 1 px padding the issue affects all apps; at 5 px padding it still affects custom-framed apps such as Opera.
The issue is triggered by snapping the window into a zone whose top edge touches the top of the screen and then single-clicking the bottom border.
Disabling Windows Snap stops the behavior entirely.
Enabling FancyZones Override Windows Snap does not stop the behavior.
inferences: Native Windows snap heuristics are clearly involved because disabling Windows Snap removes the symptom.
FancyZones geometry and custom-frame border calculations still likely matter because the custom-framed app threshold differs from standard apps.
issue_context.analysis: The report already contains the kind of layout and threshold detail a maintainer needs to recreate the bug. The missing piece is a local observation of actual window bounds and snap state under a known custom-framed application; that is a maintainer task, not a reporter task.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the complete issue body, labels, assignees, and empty live timeline.
Inspected FancyZones spacing-related unit tests, including WorkArea.Spec.cpp coverage for edited spacing and Layout.Spec.cpp spacing behavior.
Checked the current FancyZones test tree and found no focused regression around custom-framed bottom-border clicks or OS vertical snap after zone placement.

actions.label: Reproduce vertical snap with custom-frame padding

prerequisites: Use a wide or ultrawide monitor where a FancyZones zone can touch the top of the work area.
Install at least one custom-framed app such as Opera.
steps: Create a FancyZones layout whose target zone touches the top of the monitor work area.
Set zone padding to 1 px and place Explorer in the zone, then single-click the bottom border and observe whether Windows vertically maximizes it.
Raise zone padding to 5 px and repeat with Explorer and then Opera.
Repeat once with native Windows Snap disabled to confirm the issue disappears.
reproduce.expected_result: Single border clicks should only begin manual resizing and must not vertically maximize the window.
reproduce.setup_prompt: Create a simple top-anchored FancyZones layout with configurable spacing and prepare both Explorer and Opera windows for repeated zone placement.

actions.note: Local maintainer reproduction only; no upstream write is performed by this artifact.
